name: Pointed Construction Separating Convex- and Faithful-Treelike Graphs
statement: For nontrivial root-locked pointed members $(A,0^d)$ and $(B,0^e)$, put $P(A)=(Q_d\times\{0\})\cup(A\times\{1\})$ and similarly for $P(B)$, and wedge their bottom origins to form $G$. Then $G$ is cover-recursively peripheral. The induced subgraph $F$ on the two top layers and the common bottom root is faithful and periphery-free, has convex hull $G$, and contracts along its two root edges to $A\vee B$. This quotient is a forbidden pc-minor exactly when both pointed factors are root-critical.
proof: Each $P(A)$ has a root-avoiding decomposition beginning with its top layer, so the wedge theorem places $G$ in the class. The two top layers are isometric and median-stable: a majority of two vertices in one layer remains there, while a mixed triple with the common root has that root as majority. Root-locking supplies witnesses against peripheral old coordinates in $F$, and neither one-edge layer coordinate is peripheral. Contracting those layer coordinates gives the pointed wedge, whose minimality is the rooted-wedge criterion.
